title: Normalize stream-fragment protocol and introduce route capacity guards
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: Recent production incidents and an increase in OpenAI-compat traffic exposed two recurring problems: 1) inconsistent chunk/fragment semantics between proxies caused fncall handshakes to drop or duplicate events under backpressure, and 2) route-level capacity spikes allowed oversized payloads to consume downstream buffer budgets and cause transient OOMs on proxy workers. This PR standardizes an explicit stream-fragment protocol header, tightens routing precedence for capacity-limited routes, and adds soft/hard payload guards per route. Summary of changes: standardized X-Redwood-Stream-Proto header to declare chunking mode and fragment sequence markers; streaming proxy now manages an explicit buffer manager with adjustable window_ms and per-connection fragment budget; routing rules updated so capacity-guarded routes (annotated in config) are routed to isolated worker pools to prevent headroom contention; payload validation early-rejects requests above route soft limit and returns structured JSON error with OpenAI-compat error fields when appropriate; fncall/toolcall handshake now tolerates reordered fragments by buffering until end-sequence marker or per-fragment timeout; compatibility mode for the OpenAI adapter preserves prior behavior when header is absent but emits a deprecation warning header to clients; default config changes: route_payload_soft_limit_bytes=256000, route_payload_hard_limit_bytes=1048576, stream_window_ms=60. Impact and rollout plan: default rollout is canary to 5% of traffic for 48 hours with metrics on proxy buffer utilization, stream-reassembly latency, fncall error rate, and route rejection rate; a follow-up will expose these controls in the Console. Backwards-compat notes: we maintain backward behavior if X-Redwood-Stream-Proto is not present; however the hard-limit enforcement is applied regardless to protect workers. See linked Linear items for QA and rollout tasks.

release_notes: Introduce stream-fragment protocol header (X-Redwood-Stream-Proto), per-route payload soft/hard limits, and an isolated capacity-guarding routing path to prevent proxy buffer contention. Backwards compatible if header is absent; hard limits protect proxy workers.
